subject: Throughput covenant & temporary queueing grace for Q3 launch
messages:
From: Elena Martin <elena@streamlineai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@streamlineai.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary throughput covenant and queueing grace for Q3 launch

Hi Soojin,

We’re two months out from our public beta and rolling traffic projections are higher than our initial commitment in the MSA. Our engineering team expects a concentrated traffic spike over a 10-day launch window and we want to avoid throttling that would damage the UX.

Short ask: can Redwood provide a temporary throughput covenant (not a permanent SLA amendment) that guarantees an increased token throughput target for the 10-day window, and a relaxed queueing/eviction policy (a short "grace" period) while we warm our caches? We understand this may be treated as a one-off addendum and are open to a modest overage fee or short-term commitment extension.

Details we can share: launch window July 14–23; baseline reserved GPUs: 12; expected peak burst equivalent: ~18 GPUs for 48 hours (heavy inference for new feature). We’ve attached a conservative traffic forecast and can provide a small runbook with expected request distribution.

We’d like to move quickly — is this something you can review with ops and provide a proposal by May 3?

Thanks,
Elena Martin
Head of Platform Operations
Streamline AI

---
Attachment: streamline_launch_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martin <elena@streamlineai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary throughput covenant and queueing grace for Q3 launch

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear note and the forecast. Happy to help.

High-level response: we can offer a temporary throughput covenant (we’ll call it a "Launch Headroom Addendum") that provides the increased token throughput for your specified 10-day window, subject to a few operational guardrails:

- Reservation bump: we’ll provision soft-reserved capacity equivalent to +50% of your baseline (so from 12 -> 18 reserved-equivalent GPUs) for the window. This is a managed reservation — the capacity will be favored for your workloads but still subject to preemption for critical infra events.
- Queueing grace window: we can apply an "admission grace" of 300s for inflight tokens during the first 48 hours of the window to allow KV warm-up; after that, normal eviction policies resume. This is limited to the stated 48-hour warm period.
- Fairness controls: to protect platform health, we’ll enforce a per-customer max-concurrency cap and lightweight token-bucketing so a single request type cannot monopolize headroom.
- Overage/fee: standard overage rate + a one-time addendum fee. Alternatively, we can convert the temporary bump into a 3-month prorated reservation at a reduced incremental rate if you prefer predictable billing.

Operational asks from your side:
- Confirm the exact start/end timestamps for the window (UTC).
- Share the feature’s endpoint patterns (paths + typical sequence lengths) so we can pre-tune batching and kernel selection.
- Provide a short escalation contact list for 24/7 paging during the window.

I’ve looped in Ben (commercial ops) and Laura (customer SLA manager) to draft the addendum and pricing. Ben/Laura — can you take a look and aim for a draft addendum by EOD May 3?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary throughput covenant and queueing grace for Q3 launch

Soojin/Laura — quick notes before I draft the addendum:

1) Pricing options
- Option A (Managed Bump): one-time fee $12k + overage at negotiated rate during window. No long-term commitment.
- Option B (Prorated Reserve): convert to a 3-month prorated reserve to cover the bump at a lower monthly uplift (~$5k/month incremental). Customer prefers predictability; recommend including a kill-switch clause if usage doesn't materialize after 2 weeks.

2) Risk controls
- We should avoid any language that suggests zero preemption guarantees. Use "preferred allocation" and "temporary headroom" terms.
- For queueing grace we must be explicit: 48-hour KV warm window + additional 48-hour soft concurrency relaxation; anything beyond is subject to platform protection.

3) Legal checklist for addendum
- Term (10 days) + explicit start/end UTC timestamps
- Metrics: specify throughput target in tokens/sec or reserved-GPU-equivalent, and define measurement method (per-route 95th pct over 5-minute windows).
- Credits: define if an SLA failure triggers credits and how they are calculated (we should offer token-level credit, capped).

I’ll assemble a redline for the MSA addendum and include sample metrics.

-Ben
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: rw_sla_throughput_covenant_v1.pdf (draft addendum stub)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request: temporary throughput covenant and queueing grace for Q3 launch

Elena — attaching the draft addendum and two pricing routes. I’ve summarized below so you can share with your finance and infra leads quickly.

Summary (two paths):
- Path 1 (No-commit managed bump): one-time operational fee $12k, overage billed per-token during the window at negotiated rate. Headroom provisioned ~+50% reserved equivalent. Queueing grace: 48 hours KV warm, 48 hours soft concurrency tolerance.
- Path 2 (Prorated reserve): convert bump into a 3-month reserve (prorated) at $5k/month incremental; includes the same queueing grace. If daily usage < 20% of projected for 2 consecutive weeks, customer may elect to terminate the reserve (kill-switch) and receive pro rata credit.

Operational checklist (we need from you):
- Final UTC window timestamps (so we can schedule capacity reallocations)
- Endpoint patterns + request size distribution (short doc is fine)
- 24/7 escalation contacts and runbook link (or give us access to your on-call)

Next steps: once you confirm Path 1 vs Path 2 we’ll circulate the redline MSA addendum and a short runbook for on-call. If you’re comfortable with the terms we’ll aim to lock the addendum and capacity plan by May 7.

Thanks — looking forward to the launch.

Best,
Soojin
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
